content: Often, one might want to contribute a theory via a series of cumulative PRs. One way to manage this is via stacked PRs. Github has a new waitlisted feature supporting this natively. Perhaps an org admin can sign us up for the waitlist? https://github.github.com/gh-stack/
That's great! I never thought we would get stacked diffs on github
On the one hand "yay". On the other hand, this means people need to learn two CLIs, gh and git.

I went through the survey for the beta and at the end they require an "email of a Slack admin who can accept an invite for an external Slack Connect channel", which I guess means they want their beta testers to provide feedback via Slack? I decided not to go through with this for now, but if there's sufficient demand I can give it a shot.

Shreyas Srinivas said:

On the one hand "yay". On the other hand, this means people need to learn two CLIs, gh and git.

The functionality is usable entirely via the GitHub UI as well.
(So most likely for a mathematician they interact with 0 CLIs, they click some buttons in VSCode and then some other buttons in the GitHub UI)

I don't have much to complain, I learnt gh long ago. I just dislike the way github tends to push its own cli where they could just use git commands and interpret them correctly. The learning issue is more for those who dislike or fear CLIs.

git is supposed to be decentralized, but as more people learn only gh for convenience, moving away from github becomes less viable

[side note:] I used to use https://github.com/realyze/pr-train as an alternative solution for managing this.
(EDIT: at least, for the 90% of easy cases)
IMO stacked requests are always a bit messy for newbies: merges from or rebases over the upstream branch tend to require some amount of merge conflict

I believe the easiest solution to teach is

git reset --soft

or truly evil techniques with fake merges
